headline: UK inflation accelerates to 3.5% ahead of upcoming budget
summary: UK inflation rose to 3.5% in the year to September, pushed up by higher petrol and diesel prices, as government borrowing reached its highest level in a year.
why: Inflation metrics dictate central bank monetary policy decisions, including interest rate trajectories, which directly influence stock valuations, mortgage rates, and bond yields.

impacts.name: UK Consumer Goods
impacts.why: Higher inflation erodes consumer purchasing power, putting pressure on retail and domestic sectors.

why_moved: An unexpected rise in inflation changes expectations for future central bank interest rate cuts, impacting currency and debt markets.
